items.informal_name: Membership in Image of Binary Function on Sets
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {γ : Type w} {f : α → β → γ} {s : Set α} {t : Set β} {c : γ},
  c ∈ Set.image2 f s t ↔ ∃ a, a ∈ s ∧ ∃ b, b ∈ t ∧ f a b = c
items.informal_description: An element $ c $ belongs to the image of the binary function $ f : \alpha \to \beta \to \gamma $ on subsets $ s \subseteq \alpha $ and $ t \subseteq \beta $ if and only if there exist elements $ a \in s $ and $ b \in t $ such that $ f(a, b) = c $.

items.informal_name: Existence in Image of Binary Function on Sets
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_3} {γ : Type u_5} {f : α → β → γ} {s : Set α} {t : Set β} {p : γ → Prop},
  (∃ z, z ∈ Set.image2 f s t ∧ p z) ↔ ∃ x, x ∈ s ∧ ∃ y, y ∈ t ∧ p (f x y)
items.informal_description: For a binary function $f : \alpha \to \beta \to \gamma$ and subsets $s \subseteq \alpha$, $t \subseteq \beta$, there exists an element $z$ in the image of $f$ on $s \times t$ satisfying a property $p$ if and only if there exist elements $x \in s$ and $y \in t$ such that $p(f(x, y))$ holds.

items.informal_name: Membership in the Image of a Binary Function on Finite Sets
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_3} {γ : Type u_5} [inst : DecidableEq γ] {f : α → β → γ} {s : Finset α} {t : Finset β}
  {c : γ}, c ∈ Finset.image₂ f s t ↔ ∃ a ∈ s, ∃ b ∈ t, f a b = c
items.informal_description: An element $ c $ is in the image of the binary function $ f : \alpha \to \beta \to \gamma $ applied to finite sets $ s \subseteq \alpha $ and $ t \subseteq \beta $ if and only if there exist elements $ a \in s $ and $ b \in t $ such that $ f(a, b) = c $.

items.informal_name: Image of a Binary Function on Sets
items.type: {α : Type u} → {β : Type v} → {γ : Type w} → (α → β → γ) → Set α → Set β → Set γ
items.informal_description: Given a binary function $f : \alpha \to \beta \to \gamma$ and subsets $s \subseteq \alpha$, $t \subseteq \beta$, the image of $f$ on $s \times t$ is the subset of $\gamma$ consisting of all elements $c$ for which there exist $a \in s$ and $b \in t$ such that $f(a, b) = c$. Formally, this is written as $\{c \in \gamma \mid \exists a \in s, \exists b \in t, f(a, b) = c\}$.

items.informal_name: Membership in Image of Binary Function on Sets
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {γ : Type w} {f : α → β → γ} {s : Set α} {t : Set β} {a : α} {b : β},
  a ∈ s → b ∈ t → f a b ∈ Set.image2 f s t
items.informal_description: If $a \in s$ and $b \in t$, then $f(a, b)$ belongs to the image of the binary function $f$ applied to the sets $s \subseteq \alpha$ and $t \subseteq \beta$, i.e., $f(a, b) \in \{c \in \gamma \mid \exists a' \in s, \exists b' \in t, f(a', b') = c\}$.

items.informal_name: Characterization of Existence in Binary Image of Finite Sets
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_3} {γ : Type u_5} [inst : DecidableEq γ] {f : α → β → γ} {s : Finset α} {t : Finset β}
  {p : γ → Prop}, (∃ z ∈ Finset.image₂ f s t, p z) ↔ ∃ x ∈ s, ∃ y ∈ t, p (f x y)
items.informal_description: For a binary function $ f : \alpha \to \beta \to \gamma $, finite sets $ s \subseteq \alpha $ and $ t \subseteq \beta $, and a predicate $ p : \gamma \to \Prop $, there exists an element $ z \in \mathrm{image}_2(f, s, t) $ such that $ p(z) $ holds if and only if there exist elements $ x \in s $ and $ y \in t $ such that $ p(f(x, y)) $ holds.
